clue.text: Rock band come into contact with smack

blocks.note: first meaning: the American glam-rock group famous for face paint
second meaning: to touch lightly, as billiard balls do, or to give a smacker on the lips

explanation.surface: A rock band getting mixed up with heroin, smack being slang for the drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Smack looks like heroin in a rock-and-roll story, but here it is a loud kiss, and touching lightly is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The group took its name from the word, and touching lightly or planting a smacker are both everyday senses of the verb.

clue.text: Checkpoint entirely controlling import

indicators.note: the outer words control, or hold within them, the letters that are wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A border checkpoint with total control over what goods are brought into the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Import as a noun means meaning or significance, the same sense as purpose or purport, a sober synonym.

clue.text: Reiterated three points about recycling rubbish

indicators.note: recycling sends something round again, so the little word comes back the other way

blocks.note: about in the sense of concerning, as in a talk on a topic
three compass points, north, south and east, said twice

explanation.surface: Someone repeating three points about recycling household waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Recycling seems to be the subject of the talk, but it turns the little word for about back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish in the sense of foolish talk is a direct synonym for drivel or claptrap.

clue.text: Blunt objections raised over qualification

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it reads upwards

blocks.note: as in ifs and buts
Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree

explanation.surface: Someone bluntly raising objections to a candidate's qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece on top of the second. BEd is the British teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stubbed has been cut short or worn down, so it is blunt rather than pointed, as a stubbed pencil.

clue.text: Most young sheep protected by conservation organisation

indicators.note: what is protected sits inside its guardian, wrapped by the outer letters

blocks.note: female sheep
the National Trust, which looks after historic buildings and land in Britain

explanation.surface: Lambs, the youngest sheep, being safeguarded by a conservation charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most recent arrival makes something the youngest, so the superlative matches the superlative phrase.

clue.text: Sort of ladies captivated by author's belief in perfection

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version, so the letters come out rearranged
being held captive means being enclosed, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the author says 'I am', shortened

explanation.surface: Some ladies charmed by a writer's faith that the world can be perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the author or setter is 'I', so author's can mean 'I'm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is the pursuit of, or faith in, perfect standards and ideals, so the phrase describes it exactly.

clue.text: Lock in colleague's support for retired people

indicators.note: the first piece is placed inside the second, as its literal position word says

blocks.note: a lock of hair
a mate is a workmate, made possessive

explanation.surface: A colleague backing a pension scheme for those who have retired from work.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired here means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Beds rest on these padded cushions, which hold up sleepers who have turned in for the night.

clue.text: Job function reportedly introduces guidance

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so the word is wanted for its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: the trigonometric function, said out loud
a post is a position of employment

explanation.surface: Reports on what a job involves, offered as advice to newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduces' puts the sound-alike piece before the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer gives directions, and figuratively the word means any indication showing which way to go.

clue.text: Cause to be valued by objective listener

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal
the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Winning favour with an impartial listener.
explanation.walkthrough: Objective looks like an adjective meaning impartial; it is a noun meaning goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone loved or cherished by others is the core sense of this verb, usually used with 'to'.

clue.text: Claimed elite snobs must be beaten up

indicators.note: a battered thing is knocked out of shape, so the letters lose their original order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A violent claim that upper-class snobs deserve a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stated or appearing true but possibly not so is apparent or professed, which is what claimed means here.

clue.text: Singer taking part in recital tomorrow

indicators.note: the wanted word takes part in the phrase, forming a piece of the run of letters

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A vocalist who will perform in a concert the next day.
explanation.definitionFit: This voice part sits below soprano in a choir, and the word also names a singer with that range.

clue.text: Be quick to punish taking cocaine

indicators.note: taking means taking away here, so the drug's letter is removed from the verb

blocks.note: to discipline or chastise
the common abbreviation for the drug

explanation.surface: Swift penalties for anyone caught with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking reads as using the drug, but it means taking away the C.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry or make haste is to act quickly, so the verb phrase matches the verb.

clue.text: Sailors upset at popular elected government refusing to vote

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down clue a toppled word reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: able seamen, abbreviated AB
taken as written, then turned upside down in this down clue
fashionable
a winning candidate gets in
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Sailors annoyed at a popular elected administration and staying away from the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstention is formally declining to cast a ballot, so the participle matches the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Required English books' assistance to grasp French article

indicators.note: something that grasps holds another item in its hand, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
New Testament, the books of the Bible's second part
help
the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: Course requirements: English textbooks plus help with French grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: If something entails a thing, it makes it necessary, so the past form means needed or involved.

clue.text: Part of building resembling a shop?

blocks.note: a store is a shop
the adjective suffix meaning like, as in 'feathery'

explanation.surface: Asking whether one level of a building looks like a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an unusual piece: the suffix -y turns a noun into 'like that noun'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each level or floor of a building is a separate horizontal division of it, which is what the word names.

clue.text: NATO finally getting embassy to provide oversight

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the name before it, so only its closing letter counts

blocks.note: the last letter of the alliance's name
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: The military alliance at last securing diplomatic supervision.
explanation.walkthrough: Oversight looks like supervision, but here it means a careless mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out by mistake is an unintended lapse, the slip sense of the word rather than the supervising sense.

clue.text: Person who investigated difficult situations involving money

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold or include, so the troubles wrap around the cash

blocks.note: being in a hole means being in trouble
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A detective probing tricky cases that involve cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherlock Holmes is Conan Doyle's fictional detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Baker Street sleuth investigated crimes, so he is a fair example of a past investigator.

clue.text: Holiday abroad precedes epidemic

blocks.note: out and about, away from home
a short holiday is a break

explanation.surface: A trip overseas followed by a spread of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday abroad' reads as one phrase; split it, with 'precedes' putting the second word's piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spread of disease through a population is called both these terms, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Wash cloth with soft soap

blocks.note: first meaning: a small towel for washing the face, called a washcloth in the US
second meaning: flattering or evasive talk

explanation.surface: Washing with a cloth and some gentle soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Soft soap sounds like a bathroom product; it is figurative, meaning smooth talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The British face cloth shares its name with smooth evasive talk, and soft soap means flattery in the same way.

clue.text: Restrict distribution of case of alcohol with good reason

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing of something, so only its outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: to ration is to limit how much is handed out
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Limiting how much drink is handed out, for sound reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: A case of alcohol looks like a crate of bottles; it is the word's outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sensible and logical is grounded in reason, so the adjective describes acting with sound logic.

clue.text: Central elements in clue's anagram fodder

indicators.note: the clue openly names the preceding words as raw material for rearranging, a jokey self-reference

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-referential note about the key parts of the clue being material for rearrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says outright that the two words before it ('in clue', with 's meaning is) are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cores of atoms or cells are their central parts, so the plural noun matches central elements.

clue.text: Auditor's restraint irritated American manual worker

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a hearer, so the words are taken as they would be heard

blocks.note: a tie restrains, and pissed is American slang for annoyed

explanation.surface: An auditor annoyed by limits placed on an American labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: An auditor is literally a listener, so it signals sound. In the US, pissed means angry, while in Britain it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who types works with the hands at a keyboard, so manual worker is a witty literal description.

clue.text: Language used by French philosopher is out of line

indicators.note: out of line here means that the line abbreviation is taken out of the thinker plus is

blocks.note: the Greek philosopher
taken as written
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A French thinker saying something inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French philosopher' wants to be read together, but French belongs to the definition and the thinker is Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: This term names a regional dialect, originally of rural France, so it is a language spoken by some French people.

clue.text: What could be seen as our responsibility?

definitions.text: What could be seen as our responsibility

blocks.clueFragment: What could be seen as our responsibility
blocks.note: surface reading: a duty that falls to the two of us

blocks.clueFragment: What could be seen as our
blocks.note: setter's reading: break the answer after its second letter and the two little words mean 'it's down to us to pay'

explanation.walkthrough: Split the four letters into two words and they make the everyday phrase meaning 'our responsibility', as when drinks are paid for by the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty resting on someone is exactly what the four-letter word means, as in burden of proof.

clue.text: Do not recycle using material objects?

indicators.note: to do a thing can mean to fix or rework it, as in doing up a house, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction on packaging telling you not to put it in the recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction 'Do not recycle' reads as one order, but 'Do' alone works on the next two words, as in doing up a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in a concrete way means dealing in tangible, physical things rather than abstractions.

clue.text: Place where people should go on the radio

indicators.note: anything broadcast on the radio is heard rather than seen, so sound matters

blocks.note: a loo is British slang for a toilet, where one goes when one needs to

explanation.surface: A broadcast telling people where they ought to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is usually met in 'in lieu of', meaning in place of.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means stead or position, as in 'in lieu of payment'.

clue.text: Drop off tin with leak

blocks.note: the chemical symbol for tin
to ooze is to seep or leak out

explanation.surface: A tin can falling off because it is leaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep briefly, the same sense as having a nap.

clue.text: Scrutineer condemned Remain after European vote

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or ruined, so its letters are broken up
after says the rearranged word follows the other pieces, so it is sent to the end

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
the cross put on a ballot paper
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An election observer criticising the Remain side after the EU referendum vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rearranged word at the end. Remain was the side backing EU membership in Britain's 2016 Brexit referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrutineer inspects things closely, typically votes or papers, which is what an inspector or tester does.
